name: Musica
description: A star 75 parsecs away, 7.8 times the Sun's width, measured from its light.

radius.source: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 103527: radius 7.775 solar radii, implied by the fitted luminosity 34.488 solar luminosities (fractional uncertainty 0.055) and temperature

temperature.source: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 103527: effective temperature 5020 +/- 125 K, from the fit of a model atmosphere to the star's spectral energy distribution (goodness of fit Q 0.037)

gravity.source: SIMBAD's compilation of spectroscopic measurements (mesFe_h): log g 3.08 from 2024A&A...683A.125P; the 17 published values span log g 2.84 to 3.3, across which the limb law changes by at most 0.1% of the centre brightness

distance.source: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 103527: distance 75.301 pc, the paper's parallax inverted (Gaia DR1's where it revised the star's, else the Hipparcos reduction of van Leeuwen 2007; section 2.3; fractional uncertainty 0.023), at which the luminosity and radius hold

text.card: A star 75 parsecs away, 7.8 times the Sun's width, measured from its light.
text.introduction: Its brightness, measured band by band, gives 34 times the Sun's luminosity at 5,020 K, so 7.775 solar radii.
text.locator: Table 2, HIP 103527: D, Teff, L, Rad, Q

quotes.title: 18 Delphini
quotes.card: 18 Delphini, also named Musica, is a binary star in the constellation of Delphinus of the low northern hemisphere.
quotes.introduction: The primary has a Sun-like golden hue and is faintly visible to the naked eye with an apparent visual magnitude of 5.506.
